description_en: Models include Fighters and Vehicles. A rider on a bike or animal is a Mounted Fighter, not a Vehicle. Apply each rule only to its stated scope: Model, Fighter or Vehicle.

A decision may be changed before rolling dice, but a previous action cannot be undone after rolling. Measure in inches along the shortest straight line between bases, including height differences. Do not measure through solid terrain. Pre-measuring is allowed by the core rules.

Models normally have 360° vision. Check line of sight along an unobstructed straight line between their bodies, excluding bases, gun barrels and decorative parts. Weapons with Arc may target only within the specified arc.

A target is in cover if another model or terrain obscures part of its body from the shooter. Obscured bases or decorations alone do not provide cover. Temporarily ignore friendly Fighters in base contact with the shooter when checking cover.

Agree on terrain properties before the battle. Terrain no more than 2 inches high and 2 inches wide is an obstacle; if either dimension is greater, it is a structure. Impassable terrain cannot be crossed or climbed over. Vehicles cannot cross obstacles or climb structures.

Closed doors normally block movement, line of sight and distance measurement. Attacks against doors hit automatically; doors have Toughness 5. Operate a lock by using Interact at a terminal within 1 inch. The destruction threshold and normal operating distance need verification.

Distinguish D6, D66, D3, Firepower, Scatter and Injury dice. For D66, use the first D6 as the tens digit and the second as the units digit: 2 followed by 4 is 24. The D3 conversion needs verification against the general division rule.

Separate rolls differ from a roll that adds dice together. A Test succeeds on or above its target; a Check succeeds on or below its target. Add a positive modifier to a Test's rolled result or a Check's target. Round ordinary division up. A die can be re-rolled only once, and the new result must be used.

A model is Active, Engaged, Suppressed or Seriously Injured/Damaged. If states conflict, apply Seriously Injured/Damaged first, then Engaged, Suppressed and Active. These battle states are separate from campaign states such as Dead and Recovery.

Fighters are Engaged when in base contact with an enemy that is not Seriously Injured. If a Vehicle is involved, choose at the start of activation whether to Engage an enemy within 1 inch. Treat Walkers as Fighters for this purpose. Seriously Injured/Damaged models cannot be Engaged.

A Suppressed model normally performs only one action during its next activation. Engaged and Seriously Injured/Damaged take precedence over Suppressed. Track Ready, activation, Suppressed, Serious Injury, lost Wounds and other conditions with separate markers.

Every model has a type and one or more subtypes; subtypes can overlap. Vehicles and Brutes have Juggernaut. When a Vehicle, Brute or Hanger-on is removed from the roster, its equipment is removed with it rather than transferred to the Stash. Hangers-on may be excluded from random draws for the starting crew or reinforcement deck.
Beasts normally cannot Interact, Treat Ally or assist Recovery. If all friendly Fighters remaining on the battlefield are Beasts, their Leadership cannot be used for Bottle Checks.

A Champion may let friendly models within 6 inches and line of sight use its Cool for Nerve tests; a Leader's range is 12 inches. Both have Inspiring. A gang must have exactly one Leader subtype model and appoint a successor if that model dies. A Loner's Leadership may be used by the gang only when all friendly models are Beasts or Loners; for Loner Vehicles, this is explicitly stated for Bottle Checks.

Flying allows straight-line movement between levels and movement over terrain and other Fighters. Measure the actual height and route travelled. It does not allow movement through impassable terrain or an endpoint overlapping another base. Flying models suffer neither falling damage nor Suppression.

During the post-cycle sequence, a Ganger with at least 37 accumulated XP rolls for advancement, then replaces its Ganger subtype with Champion. Retain its other subtypes and original named Fighter type.

Choose whether to use Mounted equipment before crew selection; this cannot change during the battle. Mounted Fighters cannot climb walls or ladders or use a secondary weapon in close combat. Charge and Run move forwards and allow only one turn of up to 90°. Explicit exceptions, such as Nimble, take precedence.

Purchase a Pet as its master's equipment and add its cost to the master's value. Deploy it whenever its master is selected; it does not count towards crew size. It activates with each activation of its master. Outside its leash range, it takes a Panicked action towards its master. Remove the Pet if its master is removed. Pets cannot control objectives but can prevent enemy control.

During the post-cycle sequence, a Prospect with at least 13 accumulated XP gains Ganger and Specialist and loses Prospect instead of rolling for advancement. Choose one Specialisation and its free skill; increase the model's value by 15 credits. Retain its original named type and other subtypes.

When a model gains Specialist, choose one Specialisation and its associated free skill. The available list has seven entries, while another stated count is eight; missing Specialisations and skill assignments need verification and must not be inferred.

Support models are added outside the starting crew size limit and may be targeted by ranged attacks only when they are the closest model. Wyrds can use Wyrd Powers and treat the relevant power lists as Secondary skill lists.

A Hybrid chooses one of its movement subtypes at activation. Maneuverable grants one additional turn of up to 90° during Charge or Run. A Skimmer ignores difficult and dangerous terrain while moving, but must make a Dexterity test if it ends there; failure inflicts a Str –, AP –, L1 hit that wounds automatically and allows no save. Tracked ignores difficult-terrain penalties. Walkers turn freely, spend 2 inches per inch of difficult terrain and count as Fighters when Engaged. Wheeled also spends 2 inches per inch of difficult terrain.

Transport (X) requires at least one clearly defined access point and carries up to X Fighters. Fighters may deploy aboard a Vehicle in the initial deployment, but cannot start aboard a reinforcement Vehicle. Brutes and Mounted Fighters cannot embark. Passengers receive Ready markers but otherwise count as undeployed: they cannot be targeted or use abilities, and their only action is Interact. Embark with Interact within 1 inch of an access point. Disembark within 1 inch of an access point and at least 1 inch from enemies; no further Interact is allowed that activation. If the Vehicle goes Out of Action, place passengers Suppressed within 1 inch before resolving its explosion. Any passenger that cannot be placed goes Out of Action and suffers a Lasting Injury roll.
Conditions are separate from battle states, and several may apply simultaneously. Some conditions, such as Out of Ammo, apply to a weapon or individual weapon profile rather than the entire model.

An attacker targeting Fearsome in melee must pass a Willpower Check or use WS 6+ until the end of its current activation. Fearsome models ignore this effect unless the target is Intimidating. An Active model with Frenzy must Charge the closest chargeable enemy within 6 inches and gains +1 Attack. Hatred (X) re-rolls failed melee hit rolls during an activation in which the model Charges or Engages the specified enemy, or is Charged or Engaged by it. Intimidating includes Fearsome and requires an enemy attempting to Charge or Engage it to pass a Willpower Check; failure leaves the enemy in place and ends its activation. Intimidating models are immune to both fear effects.

Fighters and Vehicles at 0 Wounds are Injured/Damaged and cannot use skills; restoring at least 1 Wound removes this condition. Intoxicated worsens WS and BS by 1 and increases Cool by 1. Webbed prevents movement and gives -1 to hit; remove it by passing a Strength Check at the end of activation.

When an Insane model activates, roll a D6 and follow its insanity result. Its activation ends after that action; a successful Willpower Check removes Insane. The action depends on whether the model is Seriously Injured, Engaged or Suppressed.

Higher M, S, T, W, I, A, Ld, Cl, Wil and Int are better; lower WS, BS and Sv target numbers are better. WS and BS succeed on a D6 equal to or above the target. Mental characteristic Checks succeed on 2D6 equal to or below the target; other characteristic Checks use a D6 equal to or below the target.

Weapon profiles list short and long ranges, Strength, AP, Lethality, traits, credits and TP separately. E means Engaged; T means Template. L is the number of Injury dice rolled when Wounds reach 0 and is not equivalent to the earlier edition's Damage. Record equipment, characteristics, skills, current XP and the next advancement threshold on model cards.

Prepare in this order: challenge and stake territory, generate scenario, set up battlefield, select crews, apply battlefield effects, select Gang Tactics, then deploy. Each gang receives one basic tactic; the lower-rated gang gains one more per 200-credit rating difference. Each tactic can be used once per battle. The defender deploys first.

Each round has Priority, Action and End phases. In the Priority phase, mark all models Ready and roll off on a D6. On a tie, priority goes to the player who did not have it last round; re-roll ties in the first round. Starting with the player with priority, players alternate activating one Ready model at a time.

A normal activation grants two actions. Single costs one, Double costs two and Free costs none. Complete one action before declaring the next. Unless explicitly allowed, an action with the same name cannot be repeated in one activation, even if its action type changes.

Shoot is Single and uses a non-Heavy ranged weapon. Aimed Shoot is Double and gives +1 to hit; Braced Shoot is Double and uses a Heavy weapon. Move travels M inches, Run M+I, Charge M+D6 and Engage D6. After a successful Charge or Engage, perform Fight or Last Blow as a Free action. Reaching within 1 inch is sufficient against a Seriously Injured target.

Group Activation is Single. Select Ready friendly Fighters within 3 inches and make a Leadership Check with -1 for each selected Fighter; on success, they activate in sequence after the acting model. Last Blow targets a Seriously Injured enemy within 1 inch: roll off using D6+S, taking the enemy Out of Action on a tie or better. Traversing a duct is Double and connects positions within 1 inch of its two openings.

Reload is Single and removes Out of Ammo from one selected profile of the model's weapon. Treat Ally and Repair are Single and grant an immediate Recovery Test to a Seriously Injured Fighter or Seriously Damaged Vehicle within 1 inch. Sabotage takes a Seriously Damaged enemy Vehicle within 1 inch Out of Action on a successful Intelligence Check.

An Engaged model may Fight (Double) or Retreat (Double, I inches). A Seriously Injured Fighter may Crawl (Double, S inches), take an action granting +1 Recovery die or use Desperate Escape. A Seriously Damaged Vehicle may gain +1 Recovery die, use Desperate Escape or Freewheel (Double, D6 inches). Desperate Escape takes the model Out of Action; on a D6 result of 1–2, roll on the Lasting Injury/Damage table.

A model that began its activation Seriously Injured/Damaged makes a Recovery Test at the end. When rolling multiple Injury dice, its controller chooses only one result. If an enemy within 1 inch is not Seriously Injured/Damaged, the model goes Out of Action without rolling. One eligible friendly Fighter within 1 inch may assist for +1 die. Beasts and Vehicles cannot assist, and Vehicles cannot receive assistance.

A model need not use its full movement allowance. Fighters may follow a curved route, but Charge and Engage use the shortest route. Vehicles normally move straight forwards. Movement within 1 inch of an enemy is normally forbidden, with exceptions for Charge, Engage, Retreat, Crawl and Seriously Injured enemies. Models cannot move through other models.

Dexterity tests succeed on a D6 result of 4+; Escher receive +1. A natural 1 fails and a natural 6 succeeds. Fighters spend 2 inches of movement per inch of difficult terrain. Dangerous terrain has the same movement cost; after crossing it, a D6 result of 1 inflicts an L1 hit that wounds automatically and allows no save.

Crossing an obstacle costs additional movement equal to its height, and a model cannot end on top of it. A duct is no more than 2 inches long and 2 inches wide and requires two openings. While moving, opening or closing a door within 1 inch costs 2 inches of movement each. Unlock a locked door by using Interact at its terminal.

A Vehicle's surface may be used as terrain for movement. When a Vehicle moves, Fighters outside its designated transport area make one Dexterity test per activation. On failure, after the Vehicle moves, place them 1 inch away in the Scatter direction. Also resolve the risk of falling when within 0.5 inch of an edge.

Climbing costs 2 inches of movement per inch of height and cannot be interrupted by ending an activation. Height differences of 0.5 inch or less are crossed for free. Ladders and stairs do not double movement cost. Gaps of 2 inches or less are crossed automatically; for wider gaps, a failed Dexterity test causes a fall. Only Walkers may leap among Vehicles, and their automatic crossing threshold is their base width.

A model pushed over an edge falls if it fails a Dexterity test. Railings give Fighters +1. During a voluntary drop, a successful Dexterity test reduces the fall effect by one band. A fall under 3 inches causes Suppression; 3–6 inches causes Suppression and an L1 hit that wounds automatically and allows no save; over 6 inches takes the model Out of Action. Falling during its own activation also ends that activation.

Declare a weapon profile and an enemy in line of sight, measure range, roll to hit using BS, then resolve each hit separately. Out-of-range attacks fail. A natural 1 fails and a natural 6 succeeds. Attacks against Seriously Injured targets suffer -1 to hit. Randomly allocate hits against Engaged targets among the participants. A model hit is normally Suppressed.

Out of Ammo affects only the profile used; Reload restores one selected profile. Rapid Fire (X) allows up to X Firepower dice and inflicts hits equal to the bullet symbols. One Ammo symbol causes Out of Ammo; two or more prevent use for the rest of the battle. A failed Ammo test counts as one additional Ammo symbol. If at least two hits are scored, they may be distributed among eligible enemies within 3 inches of the original target.

If a Blast or Template hits an Engaged model, it also hits friendly and enemy models in the same engagement. Blasts affect only the same level and are resolved at the same height even after scattering. Target Priority and Stray Shots are optional rules. Target Priority requires attacking the closest enemy within 12 inches and line of sight unless a Cool Check is passed.

The Active model and enemies Engaged with it take part. The Active model chooses one primary weapon and one permitted secondary weapon; other participants use only one primary weapon. The Active model makes A primary attacks, plus one if it Charged this activation, and one secondary attack. Each inactive participant makes one attack regardless of A. A Light weapon attacks only once. Resolve attacks in descending modified Initiative order.

A successful Charge this activation gives +2 Initiative for attack order. Resolve attacks in descending modified Initiative. Ties are simultaneous: roll for the Active model first for convenience, but tied opponents still make their attacks even if those attacks take them Out of Action or leave them Seriously Injured/Damaged.
Attacks against an opponent that was not in line of sight when the Charge or Engage was declared suffer -1 to hit.

An eligible Assist gives +1 to hit; Interference gives -1. Neither stacks when several models qualify. An assisting model must be Engaged with the target and not with another model from the same enemy gang; corresponding eligibility restrictions apply to Interference.
Melee attacks use WS Tests: a natural 1 always fails and a natural 6 always succeeds. Roll separately for different weapons and targets. Light ranged weapons also use WS when attacking in melee.

If all enemies Engaged with the Active model become Seriously Injured/Damaged or go Out of Action, it may consolidate up to I inches. It may move within 1 inch of enemies during this move but must end at least 1 inch from every enemy.
Compare weapon Strength with target Toughness on a D6. Wound on 2+ if S is at least twice T, 3+ if higher, 4+ if equal, 5+ if lower but more than half T, and 6+ if half T or less.

For each successful wound, apply AP to the D6 save roll; a result equal to or above Sv saves it. Even with several save types, choose only one save per successful wound. A rule forbidding saves cannot be bypassed with another save or modifier. The target's player chooses the resolution order of simultaneous attacks.

Ranged cover grants +1 to saves at short range and +2 at long range. For a scattered Blast, assess cover from its centre. For a non-scattered Blast, assess the declared target's cover from the shooter and other hit models' cover from the Blast centre.
Invulnerable saves ignore all modifiers, including AP and cover. Natural save rolls of 1 or 2 always fail.
Each unsaved wound removes 1 Wound. When a model reaches 0 Wounds, or suffers further damage while already at 0, roll L Injury dice and choose one result. Wounds cannot fall below 0.

An Injury result applies Injured/Damaged. A Serious Injury result makes a Fighter Seriously Injured or a Vehicle Seriously Damaged, with no additional effect if already in that state. Out of Action removes the model from the battlefield and requires a Lasting Injury/Damage roll.

A model at 0 Wounds is Injured/Damaged. Restoring a positive number of Wounds removes this condition. A Seriously Injured/Damaged model becomes Active, but immediately goes Out of Action if an enemy is within 1 inch.
When a friendly model goes Out of Action within 3 inches, observing models make a Cool Check. Each observer that fails becomes Suppressed.

Resolve the end of a round in this order: Bottle Checks, victory/objectives, reinforcements. Make a Bottle Check using the highest Leadership on the battlefield only if at least one of your gang's models went Out of Action this round. On failure, withdraw one model; on a natural 12, withdraw two. An Engaged model cannot be chosen to withdraw while an unengaged friendly model remains. Withdrawn Seriously Injured/Damaged models also make a Succumbing roll.

Once at least one third of the starting crew, rounded up, is Out of Action or has withdrawn, the gang may voluntarily flee at the start of the victory check. Remove every model and automatically lose the scenario. Seriously Injured/Damaged models removed this way make Succumbing rolls.

Control an objective if at least one friendly non-Pet Fighter and no enemy models, including Pets, are within 3 inches of its centre. Ignore Seriously Injured/Damaged models. Vehicles and Pets cannot control objectives but can contest them. Only one controlling Fighter, chosen by its player, receives objective XP. If no scenario end condition is met, continue to the next round and deploy reinforcements.

Each time a model goes Out of Action, the opponent rolls D66 for the Fighter's Lasting Injury or Vehicle's Lasting Damage. Repeated results apply again. If a duplicate skill or trait restriction prevents part of a result, ignore only that part and apply the rest. Roll only once when several simultaneous causes take a model Out of Action. This is mandatory in campaigns and may be omitted in skirmishes.
Recovery prevents participation in every subsequent battle and post-cycle action of the current campaign cycle. Remove Recovery during roster updates; the model may then take part again.
At battle end, a model that is Seriously Injured/Damaged, or fled while in that state, rolls a D6: on 3+ it survives; on 1–2 it counts as Out of Action and rolls for Lasting Injury/Damage.

After a Captured result, roll a D6 for escape. On 1, the model dies or is destroyed and is deleted. On 2–4, pay a ransom of D6×10 credits during roster updates to place it in Recovery; if unpaid, delete it and transfer its carried equipment to the captor's Stash. On 5–6, it escapes and enters Recovery.

Each power has a Free, Single or Double action cost. A successful Maintain Control (Single) Willpower Check at +3 keeps a continuous power in effect until the end of the next activation; failure ends it immediately. Maintain Control as a Free action at the start of activation uses an unmodified Check and prevents manifesting other powers that activation, whether it succeeds or fails. Concentrate (Single) gives +1 Willpower to manifest powers this activation.

Manifest a power with a Willpower Check. Only one enemy Wyrd per power may attempt disruption; it must be Active or Suppressed, not Injured, within 18 inches and in line of sight. Successful disruption gives the manifesting Wyrd -2 Willpower. A natural 2 on disruption automatically prevents manifestation and causes Perils for the disrupting Wyrd; a natural 12 automatically fails disruption and also causes Perils for that Wyrd.

A natural 2 or 12 when manifesting or disrupting triggers Perils. A natural 2 to manifest automatically manifests the power before Perils; a natural 12 automatically fails manifestation, then immediately triggers Perils.

The D6 Perils table can cause a repeated manifestation followed by shock, Scatter movement, nearby weapons running Out of Ammo, Insane, a 5-inch Blast or temporary physical enhancement. On 5 the Wyrd goes Out of Action; on 6 it goes Out of Action at the start of the next round's End phase.
Weapons created by Wyrd Powers cannot become Out of Ammo and ignore Ammo symbols on Firepower dice.
Both players resolve the post-battle sequence together in this order: wrap up, reallocate territory, claim rewards, clean up and report results.
The winner gains the staked territory. On a draw, unoccupied territory remains unoccupied and occupied territory stays with its original owner.

Rewards depend on the campaign. Put equipment in the Stash and distribute it during the post-cycle sequence. When Reputation increases and decreases together, apply increases first, then decreases; Reputation cannot fall below 1.

If at least one of your gang's models remains on the battlefield at battle end, recover a dead Fighter's equipment into the Stash. Otherwise, equipment belonging to deleted models is lost. Recovery of retired models' equipment depends on their type and subtypes.
Report the participating gangs, result, territory gained and number of enemy models each gang took Out of Action to the Arbitrator.

Gain +1 XP for participating in a battle. A model's own action directly causing an enemy to become Seriously Injured grants +1 XP, or taking it Out of Action grants +2 XP. Add +1 against a Leader, Champion, Brute or Vehicle. Do not award both Serious Injury and Out of Action XP for the same enemy in the same activation. Successful Recovery assistance and objective control each also grant +1 XP; objective XP is limited to once per Fighter per battle.

Resolve post-cycle actions, collect income, then update rosters. Roster updates proceed through advancements, visiting the Trading Post, redistributing equipment and cleanup. Each model without Recovery or Critical may perform one post-cycle action.

A Leader or Champion escorts one Critical Fighter. At the start of roster updates, pay 30 credits or the patient dies. Roll a D6: 1 means death; 2–3 causes a Lasting Injury with a tens digit of 5; 4–6 gives Recovery. Before rolling, each additional 50 credits buys +1 to the result.

A Leader or Champion pays 50 credits for each selected Lasting Injury on the patient and removes it at the start of roster updates. Pay separately for duplicate injuries. Critical cannot be removed. The patient cannot perform another post-cycle action or receive Medical Escort in the same sequence.
A Leader or Champion generates one Gang Tactic.
A Vehicle pays 50 credits for each selected Lasting Damage and removes it at the start of roster updates. Pay separately for duplicate damage results.
Up to five Leaders, Champions, Gangers or Prospects may Work Territory per cycle, earning 15 credits each.

A Leader or Champion provides access to external Trading Posts and generates TP. The base and role-specific TP values conflict; the calculation needs verification before an automatic total can be used.
An eligible model trains to gain 2 XP.
Collect income and bonuses from controlled territories, plus 10 credits for each point of Reputation.
Remove all Recovery markers and remove dead, destroyed and retired models from the roster.

During the post-cycle sequence, gain one advancement for each new accumulated-XP band reached. For example, increasing from 6 to 7 XP grants an advancement. Starting XP at recruitment does not grant advancements, and XP is not spent to buy them. Add the listed credit value for every advancement.

Each newly crossed XP band grants an advancement; count every row separately even when its rank name repeats. The table begins at 1–3 XP. How the first advancement applies from 0 XP needs verification.

Roll on the 2D6 advancement table and record the characteristic improvement or skill and the value increase. A +1 improvement to WS, BS or Sv improves its target number. The permitted direction of result adjustment is inconsistent and needs verification; do not automatically allow choosing higher or lower results.
Unless explicitly excepted, advancements, equipment and bionics cannot exceed characteristic limits: M 12; WS and BS 2+; S, T, W, I, A and mental characteristics 10; Sv 3+.

Primary and Secondary skill access depends on the model type and gang. An advancement result of 12 can also select skills exclusive to a particular gang or Inner Circle, and skills normally unavailable to the model's type or subtype.

Recruitment and equipment transactions take place in the Trading Post step of roster updates. Gang equipment lists are always available; external Trading Posts require at least one Visit Trading Post action. Exclusive equipment marked E may be bought only if it appears on the model's equipment list. Each transaction spends both credits and TP; unused TP expires at the end of the step.
Items in the Stash may be sold: remove the item and receive half its credit value, with a minimum of 5 credits.

Equipment may be discarded, transferred to the Stash or given to another model. Equipment marked E must appear on the recipient's equipment list. Models owning more than three weapons require multiple equipment-set cards.

A Fighter may carry at most three weapons. Grenades count as equipment and do not use weapon slots; a weapon marked * uses two slots. Vehicle weapon limits are specified in each Vehicle entry. Each weapon can have at most one accessory.

Every model may have multiple equipment-set cards at no extra cost. An item may be shared across sets but is purchased and counted towards roster value only once. A model has one roster entry, with injuries and advancements shared by all cards. Use only one card in a battle. Random selection must prevent selecting the same model twice and must not let the player directly choose its set.

The default gang creation budget is 1,000 credits and cannot be exceeded. Unspent campaign credits remain in the Stash; unspent skirmish credits are lost. The Arbitrator may change the campaign budget.

A gang normally has exactly one Leader. The combined number of Champions, Brutes and Hangers-on cannot exceed the number of all other models. Pets are equipment and are excluded from this ratio. Correct campaign imbalances through post-cycle recruitment or retirement. Gang-specific exceptions take precedence.

Choose a successor from non-Loner Champions first, then Loner Champions, then other eligible Fighters. Within each group, decide by highest Leadership, then total XP, then player choice. The new Leader keeps its characteristics, skills and special rules and gains the type and access appropriate to its role.

A gang that completes a campaign may continue as an Enduring Gang. Its previous Leader retires, and an existing Fighter becomes the new Leader. Rehired models must be paid for and retain XP, injuries, equipment and skills. One chosen previous Triumph benefit applies only to the immediately following campaign.
Gang Rating is the total credit value of its models. Wealth adds unspent credits and the value of Stash equipment to model value. Reputation is separate; it starts at 1 and cannot fall below 1.

Record Gang Rating, Reputation, credits, Wealth, territories, Triumphs, progress and the Stash for the gang. For each model, record type, value, accumulated XP, next advancement XP, Recovery and Lasting Injuries or Damage.
A rule specifying a type or subtype applies to every matching model regardless of its name. A rule specifying a named type applies only to the entry with that name.
Collect 15 credits as income. Instead, forgo this income to discount the recruitment cost of one Ganger by 25 credits, to a minimum of 0. A starting Settlement cannot be staked or lost.

Income: 15 credits. If the gang has no Ammo-Jack, it may instead discount the recruitment cost of one by 30 credits. In a battle for this territory, each gang may perform one Reload as a Free action per round.

Income: 15 credits. If the gang has no Rogue Doc, it may instead discount the recruitment cost of one by 30 credits. In a battle for this territory, a Fighter assisting Recovery rolls two Injury dice instead of one.

Income: 15 credits. If the gang has no Hive Watcher, it may instead discount the recruitment cost of one by 30 credits. Ranged weapons cannot be used in the first round of a battle for this territory.
Income: 15 credits. If the gang has no Slopper, it may instead discount the recruitment cost of one by 30 credits. All models gain +1 Leadership in a battle for this territory.

Income: 15 credits. If the gang has no Dome Runner, it may instead discount the recruitment cost of one by 30 credits. In a battle for this territory, add D3×10 credits to the reward for completing a Side Job.
Income: 25 credits. Each player generates one additional Side Job in a battle for this territory.
Income: 15 credits. Gain +1 Reputation while controlling this territory; remove this bonus if it is lost. Visibility (X) does not apply in a battle for this territory.
Income: 25 credits. In a battle for this territory, gain 10 credits for each enemy model taken Out of Action.
Income: 20 credits. Apply Tunnel Warfare in a battle for this territory.

Income: 15 credits. While controlling this territory, gain +1 TP per post-cycle sequence and always have Trading Post access. Blast and Template weapons cannot be used in the first round of a battle for this territory.
Income: 15 credits, or forgo it to add three free Hazard Suits to the Stash. In a battle for this territory, reduce the X in Blaze (X+) by 1, for example from 5+ to 4+.
Income: 20 credits. In a battle for this territory, a natural 1 on an Agility test also inflicts a Str –, AP –, L1 hit on that model. It wounds automatically and allows no save.
Income: 25 credits. In a battle for this territory, the defender places a shrine marker within 6 inches of the battlefield centre. Fighters may control the shrine as an objective to gain XP.
Income: 20 credits, or forgo it to add two free Respirators to the Stash. Apply Visibility (18 inches) in a battle for this territory.
Income: 15 credits. Gain +1 Reputation while controlling this territory; remove this bonus if it is lost. In a battle for this territory, each player may re-roll one die once per battle.
Income: 20 credits. In a battle for this territory, Toxin (X+) weapons receive an AP adjustment of 1. The direction of the signed AP adjustment needs verification.

Income: 20 credits. In a battle for this territory, a model within a weapon's Long Range and not in cover increases its Save characteristic by 1. The distinction between Long Range and Short Range for this effect needs verification.
Income: 25 credits. In a battle for this territory, a model gains +1 XP when its melee attack makes an enemy Seriously Injured/Damaged or takes it Out of Action.

The roll-off winner chooses a battlefield edge; the opponent uses the opposite edge. The deployment distance is 12 inches. Its exact relationship to the centre line and deployment zones needs verification.

The roll-off winner chooses a battlefield edge; the opponent uses the opposite edge. The deployment distance is 9 inches. Its exact relationship to the centre line and deployment zones needs verification.

The roll-off winner chooses a battlefield edge; the opponent uses the opposite edge. The deployment distance is 6 inches. Its exact relationship to the centre line and deployment zones needs verification.
The defender deploys within 6 inches of the battlefield centre. The attacker deploys at least 12 inches from the centre.
The roll-off winner chooses a battlefield quarter; the opponent uses the opposite quarter. Each deploys in its quarter at least 9 inches from the centre.

The roll-off winner uses areas within 9 inches of a chosen corner and the diagonally opposite corner. The opponent uses the other two corners. Each gang divides its crew as evenly as possible between its two deployment zones.

Place one objective at the centre. At Check For Victory, controlling it grants 1 VP; the first player to reach 3 VP wins. If only one gang has models remaining on the battlefield, that gang wins; if neither does, the battle is a draw.

From round 3 onwards, at Check For Victory, a player wins if only their gang has a model that is not Seriously Injured/Damaged within 9 inches of the centre. If only one gang has models remaining on the battlefield, that gang wins; if neither does, the battle is a draw.

Place one objective at the centre. Starting with the roll-off winner, each player adds one more, at least 6 inches from other objectives and battlefield edges. At Check For Victory, controlling two objectives grants 1 VP; the first player to reach 3 VP wins. If only one gang has models remaining, that gang wins; if neither does, the battle is a draw.

At Check For Victory, gain 1 VP per enemy taken Out of Action this round. Gain +1 VP if it was a Leader, Champion or Brute and +1 VP if taken out by Fight, Coup de Grâce or Sabotage; these bonuses can combine. The first player to reach 10 VP wins. If only one gang has models remaining, that gang wins; if neither does, the battle is a draw. The ending point for a draw before reaching the VP target needs verification.

The attacker places an objective 6 inches inwards from the midpoint of its chosen battlefield edge; the defender does the same at the opposite edge. At Check For Victory, controlling both objectives grants 1 VP; the first player to reach 3 VP wins. If only one gang has models remaining, that gang wins; if neither does, the battle is a draw.

Starting with the defender, players alternate placing three objectives each in the opposing deployment zone, at least 6 inches apart. At Check For Victory, controlling an objective in the opposing zone grants 1 VP and removes it. The first player to reach 2 VP wins; if both have at least 2 VP, the battle is a draw. If only one gang has models remaining, that gang wins; if neither does, the battle is a draw.

A round proceeds through Priority, Action and End. Roll off for Priority; reroll a first-round tie and give later ties to the player without Priority in the previous round. Ready eligible models, then alternate individual activations starting with the player who has Priority. After activations, resolve the End phase, including fleeing, recovery and rallying.

A normal activation allows two actions. Simple actions can repeat; a Basic action cannot repeat its own name in that activation. Double actions use both actions. Move is Simple; Shoot, Aim, Stand Up and Fight are Basic; Charge is Double. Two Moves are legal, while two ordinary Shoots require a specific exception. Check state, weapon traits and skills before choosing actions.

Active and Engaged Fighters are Standing; Pinned and Seriously Injured Fighters are Prone. A Pinned Fighter can use Stand Up (Basic), then spend the remaining action. Crawl (Double) moves up to half M. Blind Fire (Double) shoots at -2 to hit. A Seriously Injured Fighter normally has Crawl available and attempts recovery in the End phase. Conditions such as Broken apply in addition to these states.

Move (Simple) allows movement up to M and normally cannot enter within 1 inch of an enemy. Difficult terrain and ordinary climbing cost twice the distance; ladders and stairs use normal distance. Charge (Double) moves M+D3 inches and a successful charge requires an attack. Gaps, jumping down and dangerous terrain have additional tests. Check the route and terrain cost before relocating the model.

Choose the weapon, profile and legal target, check range, then roll to hit using BS. Target Priority can require a Cool test to choose a more distant target unless an exception applies. An Ammo symbol on the Firepower die triggers an Ammo test; resolve the current attack before applying Out of Ammo after a failure. A Standing Active Fighter hit by a ranged attack normally becomes Pinned even if the attack causes no wound.

Apply the profile’s range-band accuracy and cover to the hit roll. Partial cover is -1 and full cover is -2; Aim (Basic) gives +1 to a subsequent shooting action in the same activation. A natural 1 normally fails. An improbable shot needing 7+ requires a 6 followed by an unmodified BS roll. These N23 cover penalties are not the N26 cover save bonus.

Resolve each hit by comparing S with T: 2+ at least double T, 3+ above T, 4+ equal, 5+ below T and 6+ at half T or less. After a successful wound roll, apply armour and AP to the save. An unsaved attack removes W equal to D. Traits can replace rolls or prohibit saves. For example, S4 against T3 wounds on 3+, and AP -1 worsens a 5+ armour save to 6+.

Choose facing, weapons, attack dice and targets, then attack using WS. Normally choose up to two Melee or Sidearm weapons, or one Unwieldy weapon. Add +1 die for charging and +1 for a legal pair, splitting dice as evenly as possible between two weapons. A Sidearm receives at most one attack die. Resolve hits, wounds, saves and damage before surviving engaged enemies make Reaction attacks. If no longer Engaged, check consolidation or Coup de Grâce eligibility.

Reduce W by D. Reaching W0 generates one Injury die, plus one die for each remaining point of that attack’s Damage. A single unsaved D3 hit against W2 therefore generates two Injury dice. Flesh Wounds reduce T by 1, with T0 causing Out of Action. A Serious Injury makes the Fighter Prone and Seriously Injured; additional Serious Injury results cause Flesh Wounds. Out of Action removes the Fighter and requires the appropriate Lasting Injury record.

Resolve Bottle tests, fleeing, recovery/restart and rallying in that order. A standard Bottle test fails when D6 plus Seriously Injured and Out of Action models exceeds the starting crew size; scenario exceptions can change the count. A Seriously Injured Fighter rolls an Injury die for recovery: Flesh Wound applies its effect and leaves them Pinned; Serious Injury leaves them injured and causes a Flesh Wound without assistance; Out of Action removes them.

Resolve end-of-battle effects, surviving Serious Injuries, captures and recovery, followed by the campaign’s resource transfers, rewards, income and post-battle actions. A standard surviving Seriously Injured Fighter avoids a Lasting Injury on 3+; a 1–2 counts as Out of Action and requires a Lasting Injury roll. Distinguish Fighters who missed this battle while in Recovery from those newly placed in Recovery. Reconcile credits, XP, equipment and the roster together.

Check the applicable table, prior-advancement surcharges, characteristic caps and skill access before deducting XP and recording the rating increase.
